chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Sabbah, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Staying awake one night due to illness is superior to a year of worship.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Superior/more virtuous (afdal) — denotes higher merit and reward in God's sight
key_terms.سَهَرُ: Staying awake (sahr) — wakefulness through the night, here involuntary due to sickness
key_terms.عِبَادَةِ سَنَةٍ: Worship for a year — a full year of voluntary devotional acts such as prayers, fasting, and night vigils
key_terms.مَرَضٍ: Illness (marad) — physical ailment that causes suffering and disrupts normal worship

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of staying awake due to illness in Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) declares that the involuntary suffering of a sick person who lies awake through the night carries a spiritual reward greater than an entire year of voluntary worship. This hadith belongs to a broader tradition in Shia Islam that recognizes illness and patient endurance as forms of divine recompense, comforting the afflicted and reframing suffering as spiritual elevation. The Imam's audience would have understood this as divine mercy — that God compensates those who are prevented from worship by circumstances beyond their control.
